author: Claude Opus subagent for Fable (curation, wording and line choices); copied unchanged into the app on 2026-11-09
license: Original project content. Positions are standard textbook ideas re-set by the curator; no book text or diagram was copied.
verification: Every position has 7 or fewer pieces. Root result, every solver move and every opponent reply were checked against the Lichess Syzygy tablebase; each line was replayed with chess.js 1.4.0; a shadow check mirrored the app's puzzle schema.
revised: 2026-11-12 (M3 fixer F3): two explanation sentences rewritten so each is true, checked against the cached Lichess tablebase and chess.js. tech-krk-mate-in-two-king-step: a rook move first misses the mate in two (Rg7 is stalemate, after Rh7+ Black's king can take the rook, the other 12 rook moves still mate but later); the old sentence said every rook move stalemates or lets the king out. tech-rook-v-pawn-king-first: the rook on h1 guards e1, the promotion square; the old sentence said it stood behind the pawn. Ids, positions, lines, ratings, themes and titles are unchanged; the source copy in reviews/claude/data is byte-identical to this one; app/data keeps the 2026-11-09 text. 2026-11-24 (version 7.3): the explanation of tech-kpkp-give-up-pawn-keep-opposition now names the key squares of the c4 pawn (b6, c6, d6) and covers the drill's third move (after Kb5, Kb7 guards b6 and c6; Kd7 leaves b6 open). Each statement was checked against the stored tablebase results (Kb7 the only draw at each step; Kc7 at the first step and Kd7 at the third lose). Ids, positions, lines, ratings, themes and titles are unchanged; the source copy in reviews/claude/data is byte-identical to this one.
ratings: Difficulty values (700-1500) are the curator's estimates on the app's 600-1800 scale, not measured from solve data.
grading: Exact match with the stored line, except that any mating final move is accepted. The README lists the plies where other moves also keep the result; the app's feedback says 'not the move this drill is practising' rather than calling them mistakes.
opponent: Opponent replies are scripted, tablebase-justified moves. There is no resisting engine ('engine defends' mode is an open owner decision, default off).
